Such a system does offer a mechanic for advancing the un-played races so that they are able to keep up to some degree with player-controlled races. As such I feel the system has many merits, and the restrictions on reclaiming godhood ensure that this mechanic can't be abused. I have a few concerns that this might lead to some very concentrated developments of some races, leading to some rather random advancement/arc progression that may undermine the ability for interactions between various players. Nonetheless, I do concur with the opinion that it is a pretty good idea.

[M] Allowing gods to play their own races... even if they are required to surrender their godhood in order to do so, at least some of the time... is probably a bad idea. Why should anyone agree to play without being a god, if this is done?

I propose instead that gods can't play races, but can influence any unclaimed races.

Reasoning: Multiplaying - playing more than one thing, especially when one can directly influence and benefit the other - seems like abad plan. However, races need advancement. The idea of a god influencing a race might not be so bad: A god proposes what a race does, other people can meta-vote to 'aye' the action if it's not stupid, and it gets done. However, unlike with 'playing' a race, the god doesn't exclusively 'own' the race - they are not the only one that gets to propose what that race does and what happens to that race. I think that the only way someone should 'own' a race in this way is if they are not also a god. That way a race doesn't get de-facto perfect loyalty or anything.

Fewer rules, races still get advanced if people care to advance them, less weirdly incestuous race/god interactions.

My thoughts, anyways.

Quick question, if you do take this approach, then do races also get a chance to propose changes for other unplayed races? While I understand the potential for abuse and conflicts of interest, but I feel it would help even out some of the influence of god players and race players.
